Output1.source_quality_basis: Credible, byte-matched primary releases support many core claims, but the final source-conditioned recommendation has material numerical or applicability defects; FAIL does not reject the underlying sources.

material_defects.claim: The determinant-product margin is treated as the discriminating numerical stability test over general affine geotransforms.
material_defects.consequence: It measures cancellation in two determinant products, not general matrix conditioning. For A=diag(1,1e-12), r=1 but kappa_2=1e12; a Y perturbation of 1e-12 changes the inverse line by 1. Both proposed thresholds accept it. The tested degrees fixture is well-conditioned, but that does not validate r as a general conditioning measure. Unresolved threshold values do not fix the test form.

material_defects.claim: A raw determinant/adjugate with only an exact-zero guard is presented under a broad six-coefficient/any-CRS domain without finite/range/precision conditions.
material_defects.consequence: Binary64 diagonal scales of 1e-200 underflow the product to zero and incorrectly refuse a well-conditioned map; scales of 1e200 yield infinite determinant and NaN inverse for an exactly representable mathematical answer (0.5,0.5). Origin 1e16 with unit scale loses a 0.5-pixel X increment despite r=1. These are reviewer counterexamples, not failures observed in the supplied eight fixtures. Mathematical totality over real numbers does not supply floating-point representability.

material_defects.claim: Corner and center differ for every nonconstant map; only the zero block must be excluded from the distinctness check.
material_defects.consequence: For gt=[10,1,-1,20,1,-1], the nonconstant rank-1 map sends both (0,0) and (0.5,0.5) to (10,20), while (1,0) maps to (11,21). The check would reject a correct forward implementation on a valid singular input. Distinctness requires A*(0.5,0.5) != 0, not merely A != 0. Convention separation remains necessary even when coordinates coincide.

material_defects.claim: Transpose/determinant is proposed as an independent inverse control whenever columns are orthogonal.
material_defects.consequence: Orthogonality alone is insufficient. For diag(2,3), the inverse at world (1,1) is (1/2,1/3), while transpose/det gives (1/3,1/2). The implemented common-norm shortcut gives (1/2,3/4). Its check tests a row dot product and does not enforce equal norms; the current rotated fixture happens to be an equal-scale, positive-determinant rotation, so its three reported checks are correct. The generalized control can falsely reject a correct inverse.

supported_optional_findings.finding: All displayed forward and adjugate formulas have the correct coefficient order. All 35 supplied point constants verify in decimal rational arithmetic and within the stated tolerances for exact binary-input arithmetic. These are useful independent point checks, not merely successful roundtrips.
Out-of-extent points are legal affine-math inputs; raster containment belongs to caller policy. Real-number totality does not guarantee finite or distinguishable binary64 outputs.

One-based labels alone do not transpose an array. World-file coefficient order is a distinct mapping plus a half-pixel origin conversion. Output2 final states the mapping accurately; Output1 repeats the seed deterministic transposition claim and Output2 metadata still does.

GDAL 3.9.0 GDALInvGeoTransform has a nonzero-diagonal/no-rotation shortcut and otherwise rejects |det| <= 1e-10*max(|linear coefficients|)^2. This is distinct from mathematical invertibility and both proposed margin thresholds. The original frozen corpus does not contain that inverse body; the supplemental release file was read, never executed. This additional source is not used to claim candidates executed GDAL or to require an external oracle when independent derivation already suffices. GCP fit tolerance in the original corpus is a different, conditional 0.25-pixel residual policy.

Both retain unvalidated production tolerance values and unevaluated external GCP execution. The specific near-singular block has kappa_2=1,999,999 and inverse operator norm 1,000,000; Output1 reported Frobenius condition about 2e6, not an absolute universal inverse-amplification factor.

incorrect_rejections.note: All supplied correct point controls are correct. These false-rejection risks are bounded counterexamples under the declared domain, not alleged observed rejections of the original eight fixtures.

The frozen columns actually match, and 22 verified point constants plus W2 inverse and W4 hand-point checks supply real independent evidence; this is an overstatement of independence, not a blanket rejection of those controls.

The receipt truthfully reports 22 mixed point checks; final/report turn that into stronger inverse evidence. All 22 constants are correct, but the inverse coverage claim is inflated.
